section_summary.extract_value: This section presents psychometric properties evaluation of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) in a single study with stratified gender groups (boys and girls). The BAS demonstrated satisfactory model fit, and concurrent validity analyses revealed a negative correlation between BAS scores and BMI for the overall sample (r = –.230) and female group (r = –.338), indicating that higher body appreciation accompanies lower BMI. Criterion validity analysis showed that normal-weight individuals had significantly higher BAS scores compared to obese individuals.

section_summary.extract_value: This section presents psychometric properties of the Body Assessment Scale (BAS), including convergent validity results. Table 3 reports correlations between BAS scores and BMI for the overall sample (n = 347) stratified by sex (Male n = 171; Female n = 176), showing a significant negative correlation for the overall sample (r = –.230, p < .001) and female group (r = –.338, p < .001), but not for males (r = –.105, p = .178). The text also discusses correlations with dissatisfaction indices and criterion validity across weight status groups.
